text.text: Spanish Football Federation's competitions committee has rescinded the yellow card shown to Real Madrid defender Ibrahima Konate during the clash with Villarreal, upholding the appeal lodged by the Royal Club. The Frenchman now faces no suspension risk ahead of the eagerly awaited Clasico against Barcelona. Konate had reached four yellow cards this season. One more booking against Sevilla on Sunday and he would have missed the trip to Barcelona. That threat has gone. With the card wiped, the French defender drops back to three yellows and a far safer disciplinary position before the big one. text.text: The Indian ODI skipper, Shubman Gill, won the ICC Player of the Month award on Tuesday. This is the fifth time he has won the prestigious award. Gill was recognised for his brilliant performances against the West Indies in September. He finished ahead of compatriot Abhishek Sharma and Zimbabwe’s Sikandar Raza.The record for the most ICC Player of the Month awards previously belonged to Pakistan’s Babar Azam, who had won it three times. Babar claimed the honour on three occasions between April 2021 and August 2023. The Indian ODI and Test skipper went past Babar after his Test exploits against England in July 2025. Gill’s latest accolade puts him level with women’s cricketer Hayley Matthews, who has also won it five times. He previously won it in January and September 2023, and then again in February and July 2025. For the uninitiated, the award considers players' performances across all formats.Gill prevailed against strong competitionIndia’s blazing T20I opener, Abhishek Sharma, posed a formidable challenge to Gill. The left-handed batter was in imperious form during the series against Afghanistan. In the first match, he scored 82 off 32 balls, then 39 off 19 in the second.

text.text: Star Indian cricketers Shafali Verma and Shubman Gill were named the ICC Women's and Men's Players of the Month for September 2026. Gill claimed the award ahead of fellow nominees Abhishek Sharma and Zimbabwe's Sikandar Raza, extending his record as the men's player with the most wins. It is his fifth such honour, following victories in January 2023, September 2023, February 2025 and July 2025. Gill's month was defined by two extraordinary innings against West Indies in the first two ODIs. In Thiruvananthapuram, he made 110 off 108 balls as India chased down 296 with more than eight overs to spare. Three days later in Guwahati, he produced an unbeaten 223 off 133 balls, an innings studded with 26 fours and eight sixes, as India hunted down a mammoth 406, their second-highest successful chase in ODI history. His century came off 62 balls, the fastest by an Indian captain in ODIs, while his double century off 117 balls was the fastest in the format's history. It was also the highest individual score in a successful ODI chase, and his 255-run opening stand with Rohit Sharma (101 off 75) was India's highest partnership on home soil. text.text: India opener Abhishek Sharma added another jewel to his crown when he became the fastest player to reach 2000 T20I runs in terms of balls faced when he took 1024 deliveries to get to that milestone when he brought up 33 runs in the 3rd T20I vs West Indies at Indore on Sunday. Abhishek pipped his former skipper Suryakumar Yadav who took 1164 deliveries to reach 2000 runs. Last month against Afghanistan, Abhishek had reached a century in 30 deliveries, the fastest by any Indian in the format. The record he took had belonged to Rohit Sharma since 2017, a 35-ball century against Sri Lanka in Indore. Meanwhile, in July, Abhishek had also become the fastest batter to smash 100 sixes in T20Is during the first match between India and England. The left-hander from Punjab surpassed West Indies’ Evin Lewis, who had smashed 100 sixes in 789 deliveries in his career. Among players from Full-Member nations, New Zealand’s Finn Allen ranks next, having reached the landmark in 871 balls in February earlier this year. text.text: Charles Leclerc and Max Verstappen have explained what happened at the start of Formula 1’s Singapore Grand Prix, where the Ferrari driver had the best launch but failed to outdo his rival. Despite starting from the dirty side of the track – which admittedly wasn’t as dirty as usual given it had rained the day before – Leclerc had his front axle nearly alongside Verstappen’s within seconds. The four-time world champion, however, drove his opponent towards the inside, to the extent that Leclerc’s front wheels briefly exceeded the white line. The Monegasque braked earlier, and Verstappen was able to retain the lead from the outside. “You don't have much time to think in those moments,” Leclerc said. “I just saw that Max had a bit of a difficult start. I had quite a good start, so I went alongside him. Then there wasn't much space anymore, but I would have done exactly the same. “Then it's quite tricky. I was on the left, a little bit behind him, couldn't see the panels on the right, so you lose a little bit all your references because that's normally on the right that you have your references to brake. When asked about it ahead of the tournament, the Spaniard quipped, "You wanted to say it's really similar to Djokovic serve (smiling). I know you want to. I wasn't thinking about making the same serve as Djokovic. But at the end, I can even see the similarities. "I think everyone has to make changes, small details. For me, the serve is something that I really want to be better every year, in every tournament. I'm just putting constant work on the serve." It certainly seemed to help as Alcaraz beat Djokovic to claim his first Australian Open crown, as the Spaniard completed the career Grand Slam at the age of 22. titles: Is Alexander Zverev a Deserving Year-End World No. 1? German’s Records Against Jannik Sinner, Carlos Alcaraz And Novak Djokovic Raise Questions

text.text: Alexander Zverev will finish 2026 as the year-end World No. 1 for the first time in his career, capping a season in which he won the French Open and US Open to claim the first two Grand Slam titles of his career. The German’s place at the top was confirmed after Carlos Alcaraz suffered a shock defeat to Zizou Bergs at the Shanghai Masters. At the same time, Jannik Sinner’s season-ending knee injury had already weakened his challenge for the year-end honour. Zverev had secured the distinction, becoming the first German and the oldest first-time year-end No. 1. Yet the achievement comes with a compelling question for tennis fans: is Alexander Zverev a deserving World No. 1 when he has struggled against the three biggest names in his way? His trophy haul is undeniable, but his record against Sinner, Alcaraz, and Djokovic adds another dimension to the debate. Zverev’s breakthrough season finally delivered the major titles that had eluded him. He beat Flavio Cobolli in a five-set French Open final in June before defeating Ben Shelton to win the US Open in September. His year-end ranking was not secured by those titles alone: Sinner’s absence and Alcaraz’s Shanghai exit proved decisive.

report.text: Club Brugge and their young forward Nicolò Tresoldi shocked Inter 4-3 at San Siro in the Champions League’s result of the night. Tresoldi, a 22-year-old Italian-born Germany Under-21s forward, scored the first three goals for the Belgian side. A Hakan Calhanoglu foul on Carlos Forbs resulted in a penalty which Tresoldi slotted in just before the half hour. Tresoldi picked up his second after capitalising on a blunder by the Inter keeper Josep Martínez and reacted faster than the Inter defence for the third with a quarter of an hour to go. Lautaro Martínez had given his team a lifeline just before the break after a move initiated by Marcus Thuram, followed by a Federico Dimarco back-heel assist. The Argentinian then gave the San Siro crowd hope again in the 81st minute by narrowing the score to 3-2, but Romeo Vermant once again exposed Inter’s defensive fragility by adding a fourth goal in the 87th minute. Ange-Yoan Bonny pulled a goal back for the home side in the third minute of stoppage time. report.text: Cristiano Ronaldo is closing on a milestone 1,000 career goals after scoring for the 981st time on Monday Cristiano Ronaldo scored as Al-Nassr won an AFC Champions League match which was delayed by an hour because of a missile alert. Ronaldo scored Al-Nassr's second goal as the Saudi Pro League champions beat Uzbekistan's Neftchi Fergana 3-1 on Monday. Kick-off was delayed after Saudi Arabia's Civil Defence issued a safety warning just 15 minutes before the scheduled start time in Riyadh, the capital city which has been the target of missiles fired from Yemen-based Houthis. Following attacks on Riyadh's airport, explosions were heard in the capital on Monday night. The Saudi-led military coalition said a ballistic missile had been intercepted and destroyed. Future sporting events could be affected by the regional conflict, including Formula 1 races in Qatar and Abu Dhabi. The 39th-ranked Belgian beat the second-seeded Spanish star 7-5, 7-6 (7/4) in the third round to land the tournament's biggest upset yet, and will play Tommy Paul next. 'Today wasn't a good match from my side. I didn't feel good,' Alcaraz told reporters, crediting Bergs for taking chances and serving big. 'In a few important moments I didn't play my best, and I would say there were a few moments that he was lucky,' the 23-year-old said of their two-hour battle. Alcaraz said he was 'disappointed' by a loss riddled with errors, which came a week after he won the Tokyo Open, adding he would return home and hit practice. 'Right now, you know, all the negative thoughts come to my mind and none of the positives, but I think I will take it, you know, the good things,' he said. report.text: On a night dominated by the apparent status of Kristaps Porzingis, the absence of the Latvian big was felt at times during the Golden State Warriors’ 101-89 win over the Los Angeles Lakers at T-Mobile Arena in Las Vegas, Nevada. Steve Kerr’s intention to spread the floor in a so-called ‘5-out’ alignment banked on players who are able to space to floor — including their center. Porzingis happens to fit that profile, while also being 7-foot-3-inches. Without Porzingis — and also not having Al Horford available tonight — the Warriors were not only small, they were bereft of shooting and spacing personnel. That was apparent at times during this game, where the Warriors were able to rally back from a significant deficit, albeit during a time when both teams’ main characters’ nights were finished (one of them, Luka Doncic, did not suit up for the Lakers). Once again, it was rookie Yaxel Lendeborg who stood out. He finished with 17 points, 5 rebounds, and 4 assists in just under 24 minutes of time on the floor.
